summary: The strongest aspect is requirements fidelity: every FR and AC is met exactly and with no unrequested extras — POST /kudos enforces required/trimmed/typed fields, the precise 80/80/280 length bounds, extra-key and non-object rejection, while GET /kudos orders by createdAt desc then id desc (matching FR-5's deterministic tie-break) with an added @@index([createdAt,id]); the Kudos model is appended below the MODEL SLOT and the module is registered in MODULES without touching the chassis, and both pnpm build and pnpm test run green. The weakest aspect is test coverage depth: all validation and ordering criteria are verified at the service layer, but there is no true HTTP/e2e test asserting the 201/200 status codes or that createdAt serializes to an ISO-8601 string, and AC-8 (persistence across restart) is not exercised against real SQLite since an in-memory stub reimplements the sort. The overall 9 reflects a clean, idiomatic, fully-conformant delivery whose only shortfalls are the missing end-to-end/restart tests and a few minor (body as any) casts in otherwise well-structured validation code.
